findings.summary: A value-channel arm whose constructor sub-pattern is not a single literal constructor (an or-pattern, a record/lazy pattern) is classified as a CATCH-ALL, so the scope closes every error the head call can return — including ones the arm demonstrably does not match. Reproduced: an error is silently dropped.
findings.evidence: lib/arch_index/arch_index_errch.ml:171-179 — `| n, _ when n > 0 -> (match List.nth_opt sub (n - 1) with | Some subpat -> let path = match literal_ctor_path_of_pat ... with Some pth -> Some pth | None -> None (* non-literal argument pattern: catch-all for this ctor *) in Some (path, pat_bound_idents subpat)`; the caller turns `None` into a channel-wide catch-all at lib/arch_index/arch_index_cmt.ml:1500-1503 — `if closing then (match caught_opt with | None -> catch_all := true | Some p -> caught := p :: !caught)`. REPRODUCED on /mnt/ssd-external-2to/arch-index-runs/rev-or with `type err = A | B of int | C`, `f` returning all three, and `let g1 () = match f 0 with Error (A | B _) -> Ok 0 | ok -> ok`: `arch-query may-fail g1 --channel result` answers `BOUNDED: {}` while the control `let g3 () = match f 0 with Error A -> Ok 0 | ok -> ok` correctly answers `BOUNDED: {Oc_a.B, Oc_a.C}`. `Oc_a.C` is omitted from g1's set although `f`'s `Error C` reaches the `| ok -> ok` arm and is re-returned.
findings.fix: Make `classify_value_pat` return a LIST of caught paths rather than an `option`: for `Tpat_or` of literal constructors return the union; for `Tpat_construct` whose sub-pattern at `arg_pos` is an or-pattern of literals return that union. Only `Tpat_any` and `Tpat_var` (which genuinely match anything) may yield a catch-all. Any other unrecognised sub-pattern must make the arm NON-closing (contribute nothing), never catch-all — that is the sound direction. Add tezt cases for `Error (A | B) -> ...` and `Error A | Error B -> ...`.

findings.summary: Re-indexing into an existing database does not clear any exception/error-channel table: exn_scopes and exn_origins DOUBLE, call_exn_scopes keeps the previous run's links against reused call ids, and the run exits 1. Stale scopes then close calls they never covered — an unsound subtraction in a database the tool reports as merely 'incomplete'.
findings.evidence: lib/arch_index/arch_index_support.ml:38-53 — `schema_tables_to_drop = ["module_deps"; "type_usage"; "type_constructors"; "type_fields"; "types"; "calls"; "functions"; "modules"; "producer_runs"]`, listing none of `exn_scopes`/`exn_origins`/`exn_scope_catches`/`call_exn_scopes`/`exn_rebinds`/`exn_edges`/`channel_carriers`; and lib/arch_index/arch_index.ml:298 `exec_exn db "PRAGMA foreign_keys = OFF"` runs immediately before the drop loop, so dropping `calls` cascades to nothing. REPRODUCED: two consecutive runs of `arch-callgraph-ocaml --build-dir=_build/default/lib/arch_index --db-path=/tmp/f.db --schema-path=architecture-schema.sql` gave run1 `exn_scopes=267, exn_origins=667`, run2 `exn_scopes=534, exn_origins=1334`, with `ERROR: 384 statement(s) failed during indexing` / `call_exn_scopes: 384 row(s) rejected` and exit code 1. `channel_carriers`/`exn_edges` stay at 135/146 only because their inserts are `INSERT OR IGNORE` — their `function_id`/`call_id` now point at rows from the previous run.
findings.fix: Add `channel_carriers`, `exn_edges`, `call_exn_scopes`, `exn_scope_catches`, `exn_origins`, `exn_scopes`, `exn_rebinds` to `schema_tables_to_drop`, ordered dependents-first as the existing list is. Add a tezt that indexes the same db_path twice and asserts identical row counts and exit 0 (the suite has such a test for `analysis_coverage` — 'coverage-matrix: re-running replaces rather than accumulates rows' — but none for the exn tables).

findings.summary: The self-index golden is stale, so CHECK-6 / AC-20 fails and CI's self-index smoke job is red — the exact regression the reviewer brief's 'stale-golden caveat' warns about.
findings.evidence: test/fixtures/self-index-stats.txt:2-3 records `functions: 733` / `calls: 4834`; a clean `dune build` followed by `arch-callgraph-ocaml --build-dir=_build/default/lib/arch_index --db-path=/tmp/rev.db --schema-path=architecture-schema.sql` on this worktree produces `functions: 735` / `calls: 4842`, and `sqlite3 /tmp/rev.db "SELECT ..." | diff test/fixtures/self-index-stats.txt -` exits 1. briefs/error-channels-impl.md:79 claims 'self-index golden re-measured: 23 modules / 733 functions / 4834 calls' — that measurement no longer matches the tree.
findings.fix: Regenerate per docs/adr/001-self-index-golden.md and diff the function-name lists old vs new before committing, so every delta is attributed.

findings.summary: The branch is NOT merged up to the current origin/main: it sets current_schema_version = "1.6" while origin/main is already at "1.7", and it reverts main's top_reason/top_anchor work. FR-034 (base+1, unique docs/schema.md row) cannot be certified from this tree, and the merge resolution review item (b) has to be redone.
findings.evidence: lib/arch_index/arch_index_db.ml:52 `let current_schema_version = "1.6"` versus `git show origin/main:lib/arch_index/arch_index_db.ml` line 52 `let current_schema_version = "1.7"`. `git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/main HEAD` fails (origin/main = 003e951 'chore(ledger): close the ledger for top-anchor-taxonomy'). `git diff origin/main` consequently shows this branch REMOVING main's content: docs/schema.md loses the `1.7` row and the arch_load `1.2` row, and lib/arch_index/arch_index_db.ml:392-420 drops the `?(top_reason = None) ?(top_anchor = None)` parameters from `insert_call_rowid`/`insert_call` — precisely the parameter-union conflict class the brief flags.
findings.fix: Merge current origin/main, keep BOTH sides' parameters on insert_call_rowid/insert_call, restore main's docs/schema.md 1.7 and arch_load 1.2 rows, and re-derive current_schema_version as 1.7+1 = 1.8 with its own docs/schema.md row (1.6 is currently unclaimed on main, so either 1.6 or 1.8 works, but the constant and the table must agree and no other row may claim it). Re-run CHECK-6 after the merge, including the golden.

findings.summary: The porting contract tells other-language implementers to emit exn_edges roles that the OCaml producer never writes and the query layer never reads. A Go/Rust/TS adapter that follows the table verbatim would emit rows that are silently ignored and would not emit the only role that actually feeds the solver.
findings.evidence: docs/error-channels-porting.md:33-35 — 'transform ... `exn_edges` `role='transform_add' | 'transform_replace'`', 'converter ... `role='convert'`', 'sink ... `role='sink'`'. The producer has exactly one `insert_exn_edge` call site, lib/arch_index/arch_index.ml:833 `Arch_index_db.insert_exn_edge db stmt_edge ~call_id ~channel ~role:"propagates"`, and the query reads exactly one role, lib/arch_tools/arch_exn.ml:268 `JOIN exn_edges ee ON ee.call_id=c.id AND ee.role='propagates' AND ee.channel=?`. Transforms, converters and sinks are instead realised as `exn_origins` rows plus `sunk_ords` suppression of the propagates edge (lib/arch_index/arch_index_cmt.ml:1911, :1932, :1954, :2186).
findings.fix: Rewrite §1's Recorded-as column to describe what the reference implementation actually does: a transform's added identity is an `exn_origins` row on the target channel; a `replace` transform and a sink are the ABSENCE of a `propagates` row for that call (plus, for replace, an origin for the mapper's literal return); a converter is a catch-all `exn_scopes` row on the `from` channel plus an `exn_origins` row on the `to` channel. Either implement the other roles or state in the doc (and the schema comment) that they are reserved and currently unused.

findings.summary: `lift` and `unwrap` are TYPE paths but are registered in the validator's VALUE-path set, which only `note_value_path` ever flips. They therefore always report 'matched nothing', and `--errors-strict` always exits 1 for any config that declares either — including the shipped Tezos profile, whose entire purpose is `--errors-profile tezos` runs.
findings.evidence: lib/arch_index/arch_errors_config.ml:396-403 — `let declared_value_paths (c : channel) = List.map fst c.origins @ c.lift @ c.unwrap @ ...`; `create` (:405-417) seeds `values` from that list, and only `note_value_path` (:419) sets those flags, while the walker reports type occurrences through `note_type_path` (:427). profiles/tezos-errors.toml:28 `unwrap = ["Tezos_protocol_environment_*.Error_monad.trace"]` and :37 `lift = ["Lwt.t", "Tezos_protocol_environment_*.Lwt.t"]`. REPRODUCED on /mnt/ssd-external-2to/arch-index-runs/rev-cfg with a channel declaring `unwrap = ["wrapper"]` and `lift = ["Lwt.t"]` over a corpus that genuinely uses `wrapper` as the unwrap container: `arch-errors: channel mych: 'Lwt.t' matched nothing` / `arch-errors: channel mych: 'wrapper' matched nothing`, and with `--errors-strict` `arch-errors: --errors-strict: 21 declaration(s) matched nothing`, exit 1.
findings.fix: Move `c.lift` and `c.unwrap` out of `declared_value_paths` and into the type-path set seeded in `create`, and flip them from `note_type_path` (the carrier check already resolves them through `strip_wrapper`, so the walker sees them as `Tconstr` paths). Add a tezt asserting `--errors-profile tezos --errors-strict` on a Tezos-shaped fixture exits 0.

findings.summary: Every console example in the user guide is fabricated or reformatted: the tool renders box-drawing tables, not the plain/pipe-delimited text shown, and the §1/§3 numbers do not reproduce with the command the doc prints. A user guide that lies is worse than no guide.
findings.evidence: docs/error-channels.md:24-29 shows `arch-callgraph-ocaml --build-dir=_build/default ...` then `of_toml: UNBOUNDED (⊤): {} / reason: external Otoml.Parser.from_string_result / reason: unknown_exn_value #77:unknown`. Running exactly that on this worktree gives a boxed table and `unknown_exn_value #208:unknown`; the `#77` node id reproduces on NO database I built (`#79` on the lib/arch_index-scoped db, `#208` on the whole-repo db). docs/error-channels.md:112-122 shows `error-stats --channel result` printing `channel|result / nodes|31 / bounded|5 (16.1%) / ... / origins|44 / escaping_origins|44`; the real output is a boxed table, the `--build-dir=_build/default` db gives `nodes 58 / bounded 14 (24.1%) / unbounded.external 4 / unknown_exn_value 39 / origins 96`, and two rows the doc omits entirely (`scopes`, `fixpoint_seconds`) are always printed. The 31/5/16.1%/44 figures come from a `--build-dir=_build/default/lib/arch_index` database, not the command shown. docs/error-channels.md:204 repeats the mismatched figure: 'On this repository the `result` channel bounds 16.1 % of carriers' (actual 24.1 % for the repository, 16.1 % for lib/arch_index alone).
findings.fix: Re-capture every ```console block verbatim from a real run, including the box drawing, and make the command shown be the command that produced the output. State the build-dir scope wherever a percentage is quoted. If the boxes are considered too noisy for docs, add a plain-output flag and use it in the examples rather than hand-editing the output.

findings.summary: `--errors-strict` promotes the built-in result/option channels' own Stdlib path misses to fatal, so it exits 1 on essentially any project that has an arch-errors.toml but does not happen to call Stdlib.Result.fold, Option.get, etc. The flag is documented as the CI setting and is unusable as one.
findings.evidence: lib/arch_index/arch_errors_config.ml:465 `List.iter note_miss (declared_value_paths c)` runs for every channel; `builtin_names` (lib/arch_index/arch_index.ml:547-552) exempts built-ins only from the FATAL carrier-type check at arch_errors_config.ml:446, not from the per-path warnings, and :481 `if strict && warnings <> [] then Error ...` promotes all of them. REPRODUCED: a fixture with one small user channel emitted 19 built-in warnings (`arch-errors: channel result: 'Stdlib.Result.fold' matched nothing`, `channel option: 'Stdlib.Option.get' matched nothing`, …) and `--errors-strict` exited 1 with 'arch-errors: --errors-strict: 21 declaration(s) matched nothing'. specs/error-channels.md AC-15 scenario 2 expects strictness to fire on the USER's typo'd path.
findings.fix: Restrict `--errors-strict` (and ideally the warnings themselves) to channels not in `builtin_names`, mirroring the existing exemption for the fatal carrier check. docs/error-channels.md:188 should say which declarations strictness covers.

findings.summary: A value-channel scope's local id is resolved against the node the CALL belongs to, not the node the SCOPE was created in. When the covered call lives in a promoted lambda (the declared-handler / converter thunk idiom), the lookup either misses or silently resolves to that lambda's OWN scope with the same local id — a handler closing a call it never covered.
findings.evidence: lib/arch_index/arch_index_cmt.ml:2873-2879 — `| Some neg -> let local_id = -neg - 1 in { c with exn_scope = Hashtbl.find_opt errch_scope_ids (c.caller_name, local_id) }`, where `errch_scope_ids` is keyed by `(node, s.s_id)` (:2836) and `s.s_id` comes from the per-context accumulator `(!cur).lerrch` (lib/arch_index/arch_index_errch.ml:237-251, `acc.next_id` restarts at 0 for every node — a fresh `Arch_index_errch.create ()` per `new_ctx`, arch_index_cmt.ml:867). `resolve_guarded_call` (:1209-1216) deliberately peels a thunk literal and resolves the call INSIDE it, whose `caller_name` is the lambda node (`Texp_function` promotes to a new ctx at :1329-1334) while the scope was added to the enclosing node's accumulator at :1855 / :1873.
findings.fix: Carry the scope's owning node in `errch_call_scope` (it is already a tuple: store `(channel, owner_node, local_id)`) and look up `errch_scope_ids (owner_node, local_id)`. That both removes the collision and makes the 'converters only close within the same CFG node' residual an explicit, intentional decision rather than an accident of the key.

findings.summary: FR-028's `inferred_bind` ⊤ is only raised for `Texp_apply`. An undeclared bind-shaped operator used through `let*`/`and*` syntax (Texp_letop) produces no ⊤ witness at all, so a custom binder that rewrites errors is silently assumed transparent.
findings.evidence: lib/arch_index/arch_index_cmt.ml:1616-1640, the `Texp_letop` branch, walks `let_.bop_exp`, each `ands[i].bop_exp` and `body`, and records the operator calls via `add_path_call` (:1628-1632) — which calls `add_call` with no `~callee_ty` (:1090-1107), so no channel candidacy — but never consults `Arch_index_errch.bind_shape_channel`. The only `bind_shape_hit` computation is inside `Texp_apply`, at :1824-1836. specs/error-channels.md FR-028: 'An undeclared operator whose type has bind shape over a carrier MUST produce ⊤ inferred_bind with the site'; US-2.13's tezt only exercises the `f () >>=? fun x -> Ok x` application spelling (tezt/tests/error_channels.ml:120-122).
findings.fix: In the `Texp_letop` branch, run `bind_shape_channel` on `let_.bop_op_type` (and each `and*`'s) and, when it names a channel that is not in that channel's declared `binds`, record the same `inferred_bind` origin the apply path records at :1960-1967. Add the `let*` spelling to the US-2.13 tezt.

findings.summary: Widening `head_qualified_name` to `Head_local` means a declared path spelled as a BARE name matches the same-named local function in EVERY module of the corpus, not just the one the config author meant. For `handlers` and `sinks` that is an unsound close/discard; the justification recorded is an assumption about configs, not a property of the code.
findings.evidence: lib/arch_index/arch_index_cmt.ml:919-923 — `let head_qualified_name = function | Head_qualified (Some m, n) -> Some (m ^ "." ^ n) | Head_qualified (None, n) -> Some n | Head_local n -> Some n | _ -> None`, with the comment at :912-918 justifying it as safe 'since no existing declared path is spelled that way'. `Head_local n` carries the bare definition name (`local_fn_name`, :1022-1026), so a config line such as `sinks = ["ignore_error"]` or `handlers = [{path = "value"}]` matches any module's local `ignore_error`/`value`. The project's own tezt fixture depends on this behaviour (tezt/tests/error_channels.ml:61 `sinks = ["never_matched"]`, :59 `transforms = [{path = "add_err", ...}]`), so the bare spelling is the documented way to declare same-module paths.
findings.fix: Qualify `Head_local` with the caller's module before matching (the module is known at the call site) and require config paths to be module-qualified, or keep the bare match but restrict it to the roles where over-matching is over-approximating (`origins`, `transforms mode=add`) and forbid it for `handlers`/`sinks`/`converters`. Document whichever rule is chosen in docs/error-channels.md §4.

findings.summary: `discover_profile` prefers a `profiles/` directory inside the ANALYSED project over the shipped one, and then walks six ancestors of the executable — which on an installed layout adds `$HOME/profiles` and `/profiles`. A repository under analysis can therefore supply the rules that decide what the analysis subtracts.
findings.evidence: lib/arch_index/arch_index.ml:119-127 — candidates are `ARCH_ERRORS_PROFILES_DIR`, then `Filename.concat (Filename.concat project_root "profiles") file`, then `List.map (fun d -> Filename.concat (Filename.concat d "profiles") file) exe_ancestors`, with `exe_ancestors = exe_dir :: up [] exe_dir 6` (:109-117). REPRODUCED: dropping `profiles/tezos-errors.toml` into an analysed fixture made `--errors-profile tezos` print `arch-errors: using profile /mnt/ssd-external-2to/arch-index-runs/rev-cfg/profiles/tezos-errors.toml` and exit 0, in place of the shipped `.../wt-exn/profiles/tezos-errors.toml` it had used a moment earlier. A profile controls `handlers`, `sinks` and `converters`, i.e. exactly what gets subtracted from a may-fail set, so an attacker-authored profile makes the analysis under-report.
findings.fix: Order the shipped/exe-relative candidates BEFORE the analysed project's `profiles/`, or drop the analysed-project candidate entirely and require `--errors-config` for a project-local file (which is already the documented per-project mechanism). Cap the exe-ancestor walk so it cannot reach `$HOME` or `/` (stop at the first ancestor that is a filesystem root or the user's home). Keep printing the resolved path, and consider printing the config digest alongside it.

findings.summary: `may-fail --channel all` prints one unlabelled block per channel, so two ⊤ verdicts on different channels are indistinguishable. The spec asks for 'one block per emitted channel' and the whole feature exists to keep channels apart.
findings.evidence: bin/arch_query/arch_query.ml:716-718 — `| Some "all" -> need_known "function" a ; List.iter run_one (channels_of_contract t)`; `run_one` emits the same verdict table for each channel with no channel identification. Observed on /tmp/rev.db: `may-fail of_toml --channel all` prints `of_toml: UNBOUNDED (⊤): {}` twice with different reason lists and then `of_toml: NOT_A_CARRIER(option)` — only the third block names its channel, and only because NOT_A_CARRIER embeds it.
findings.fix: Prefix each block with the channel name (a header row or a `channel: <name>` line). FR-029's byte-identity constraint applies to `raises`/`raisers-of`/`exn-stats` and to `may-fail <fn> --channel exception`, not to `--channel all`, so a label here breaks nothing — the `raises` == `may-fail --channel exception` identity was verified byte-for-byte and stays intact.

findings.summary: `error_config_digest` is MD5, not the SHA-256 the spec specifies.
findings.evidence: lib/arch_index/arch_errors_config.ml:383 — `Digest.to_hex (Digest.string (chan_str ^ "##" ^ sum_str))`; OCaml's `Digest` is MD5. specs/error-channels.md Clarifications, 'Discovery, precedence, digest': '`error_config_digest` = SHA-256 of the canonical serialisation of the *effective merged* config (sorted keys)'.
findings.fix: Either use a SHA-256 implementation (the switch already carries digestif/mirage-crypto transitively) or amend the spec and docs to say MD5 and why. The stability/change properties the tests assert (arch_errors_config.ml:553-567) hold either way; this is about the contract saying what the code does.

findings.summary: FR-024 PARTIAL: `error_config_digest` is MD5 (OCaml's Digest), not the SHA-256 the spec's Discovery/precedence/digest clarification specifies.
findings.evidence:
lib/arch_index/arch_errors_config.ml:334 comment "Digest — canonical structural serialisation, MD5 hex"; :383 `Digest.to_hex (Digest.string (chan_str ^ \"##\" ^ sum_str))` (OCaml's Digest is MD5).
Observed value is 32 hex chars: `sqlite3 spec.db "select value from comment_db_meta where key='error_config_digest'"` -> `21edc0e390cb898e022dcfcc73bc3d20`.
specs/error-channels.md:26: "`error_config_digest` = SHA-256 of the canonical serialisation of the *effective merged* config (sorted keys)".
The substantive properties DO hold (verified by running the producer three times): effective-merged (builtin-only 21edc0e3... vs builtin+user c0421a35...), stable across reformatting (a reformatted equivalent file reproduced c0421a35...).
findings.fix: Use SHA-256 (e.g. digestif/mirage-crypto already in the switch) or amend the spec clarification to say 'a stable content digest' rather than naming SHA-256.

findings.summary: The porting guide claims every one of the six tables carries a `channel` column; two of them do not, and one of those (call_exn_scopes) is additionally single-scope-per-call, which a porter must know or they will design a multi-channel scope model that cannot be stored.
findings.evidence: docs/error-channels-porting.md:113-114 — 'write `exn_origins`, `exn_scopes`, `exn_scope_catches`, `call_exn_scopes`, `exn_edges`, `channel_carriers`, all carrying `channel`'. architecture-schema.sql:366-369 `CREATE TABLE ... exn_scope_catches (scope_id INTEGER NOT NULL ..., exn_path TEXT NOT NULL)` — no channel column; :389-392 `CREATE TABLE ... call_exn_scopes (call_id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES calls(id) ..., scope_id INTEGER NOT NULL ...)` — no channel column and one row per call. The OCaml producer works around the latter by letting an exception-channel link win over a value-channel one (lib/arch_index/arch_index_cmt.ml:509-520, :2187-2193).
findings.fix: Correct the sentence to name the four tables that carry `channel` (exn_origins, exn_scopes, exn_edges, channel_carriers) and state that exn_scope_catches inherits its channel from its scope and that call_exn_scopes holds at most ONE scope per call — with the reference implementation's tie-break rule spelled out, since a porter has to pick the same sound direction.

findings.summary: AC-16 claims US-2 scenarios 1–13 are covered by tezt, but the fixture covers only a subset: the head-call-only rule (scenario 9, the reviewer brief's audit item 2) has no test at all, and neither do scenarios 6, 11, 12, nor any or-pattern arm — the case that turns out to be unsound.
findings.evidence: tezt/tests/error_channels.ml:8-14 states the file's own scope as 'US-2 scenarios 1, 2, 3, 4, 10 and US-3 scenarios 1, 3'. The fixture (:68-158) contains no `wrap`/`nest` pair (scenario 9), no `ignore`/`let _` sink pair (scenario 6), no Tezos-shaped `let*`/`record_trace`/`catch`/`error_when` group (scenario 11), no mixed exception+value function (scenario 12), and no arm with an or-pattern. specs/error-channels.md AC-16: 'scenarios 1–13 → tezt (producer + query sections)'.
findings.fix: Add the missing scenarios, starting with 9 (the sound-direction rule the whole propagation model rests on) and the or-pattern arm from the CRITICAL finding. Manual verification for 9 on an ad-hoc fixture did show the sound direction — `let nest () = match wrap (f 0) with Error (B _) -> Ok 0 | ok -> ok` answered `BOUNDED: {Oc_a.A, Oc_a.B, Oc_a.C}`, i.e. f's errors survive the head-only coverage — but nothing in the suite locks that in.

findings.summary: `path_matches`'s `*` is a full glob that crosses `.` boundaries, although it is documented and used as a UNIT-component wildcard. In `handlers`/`sinks`/`converters` an over-matching pattern closes or discards calls it was never meant to cover.
findings.evidence: lib/arch_index/arch_errors_config.ml:105-116 — `| '*' -> go (pi + 1) si || (si < alen && go pi (si + 1))`, with no exclusion of `.`; the comment at :100 calls it '[*] in the UNIT component of a profile path'. profiles/tezos-errors.toml:8 documents the intent ('UNIT-component wildcard: "Tezos_protocol_environment_*"') and uses it in `handlers`/`sinks`/`converters` (e.g. :98 `{ path = "Tezos_protocol_environment_*.Error_monad.catch_f", from = "exception", ... }`, :115-124 `sinks`).
findings.fix: Make `*` match only within one dot-separated component (stop the skip branch at `.`), which is what both the comment and the profile intend. If cross-component matching is wanted, give it a distinct spelling (`**`) and keep it out of the closing roles.

findings.summary: The porting guide and the user guide disagree with the tool on the ⊤ reason string: both docs say `unknown_error_value`, the query prints `unknown_exn_value`. A porter checking their output against the doc will think their rows are wrong.
findings.evidence: docs/error-channels-porting.md:46 'the query renders it ⊤ `unknown_error_value` with a witness' and :139 'An unresolvable identity is ⊤ `unknown_error_value` *with a witness*'. lib/arch_tools/arch_exn.ml:36 `| Unknown_exn_value -> "unknown_exn_value"`, and the observed output is `reason: unknown_exn_value #208:unknown`. docs/error-channels.md:29 uses the correct spelling, so the two guides also contradict each other.
findings.fix: Use `unknown_exn_value` in both docs, or rename the reason kind now (before external consumers depend on it) and update every doc and the spec's `unknown_error_value` occurrences together.

findings.summary: The `exn_rebinds` alias table is applied to VALUE-channel paths too, so a module that has both `exception A = B` and a variant constructor `A` would have its value-channel error identity rewritten to the exception's target.
findings.evidence: lib/arch_tools/arch_exn.ml:275-285 loads `rebinds` from `SELECT alias_path, target_path FROM exn_rebinds` with no channel qualification (the table has none), and it is applied unconditionally to caught paths (:292 `let p = canon_r (text p)`), to origin paths (:422 `join acc (Known (SS.singleton (canon t p)))`) and inside `close` (:400 `SS.mem (canon t p) caught`) for every channel. Polymorphic-variant identities are safe by construction (they carry a leading backtick, arch_index_errch.ml:111-112), so the exposure is limited to ordinary constructor paths that collide with an exception alias path in the same module.
findings.fix: Skip `canon`/`canon_r` when `t.channel <> "exception"`, or give `exn_rebinds` a channel column. Cheap and removes the class entirely.

findings.summary: Head-call resolution keys on `Location.t`. Two distinct applications sharing a location — routine in ppx-expanded code — collide in `apply_head_ord`, so a handler scope or a sink can attach to the wrong call.
findings.evidence: lib/arch_index/arch_index_cmt.ml:887 `let apply_head_ord : (Location.t, int) Hashtbl.t = Hashtbl.create 32`, written with `Hashtbl.replace apply_head_ord hloc ord` (:944-946) and read by `resolve_head_call` (:903-907). The module already acknowledges ghost/ppx location collisions elsewhere and handles them with an ordinal (`lambda_name`, :1005-1012); this table has no such disambiguation. Attaching a scope to a call it does not cover is a subtraction on the wrong edge.
findings.fix: Key on the physical expression identity, or apply the same `#N` collision ordinal used for lambda names and refuse to resolve a head when the location is ambiguous (refusing is the sound direction: an unresolved head simply propagates).

findings.summary: A scope manifest belonging to the PREVIOUS feature is added by this branch. No deterministic scope gate ran, and this is the one file in the diff that is not about error channels.
findings.evidence: briefs/exn-raise-sets-manifest.txt:1-8 — `base=69e5c3d07251abbb514cb73c6000d146a284d2ef` followed by `dirty=briefs/exn-raise-sets-implementer.md`, `dirty=briefs/exn-raise-sets-intake.md`, … — the manifest of the exn-raise-sets task. findings.summary: FR-029's 'the exception channel's rows are unchanged' does not hold once a profile declares converters: a converter writes a catch-all scope tagged channel='exception', which the exception solver reads and subtracts. This is the intended semantics of Tezos `catch`, but it contradicts the MUST as written.
findings.evidence: lib/arch_index/arch_index_cmt.ml:1866-1877 — `| Some (from_, to_, argpos, err) -> ... Arch_index_errch.add_scope (!cur).lerrch ~channel:from_ ~catch_all:true ~caught:[] ~loc:expr.exp_loc`, with `from_ = "exception"` for profiles/tezos-errors.toml:96-98; that scope is inserted into `exn_scopes` with its own channel at :2830-2833, and lib/arch_tools/arch_exn.ml:314 reads `exn_scopes WHERE channel=?` with channel='exception'. briefs/error-channels-impl.md:81 records the resulting delta ('proto_alpha exception scopes 18 → 19, the converter's catch-all at script_repr.ml:264'). Verified that the frozen half still holds: with built-ins only, `raises of_toml` and `may-fail of_toml --channel exception` are byte-identical (`diff` empty), and `dune test --root . --force` is 110/110 exit 0.
findings.fix: Amend FR-029 to 'unchanged for the built-in configuration; a declared converter from the exception channel deliberately adds an exception-channel scope', and keep the numeric anti-regression gate scoped to runs without a converter-bearing profile — otherwise the gate and the feature are in permanent conflict.

findings.summary: call_exn_scopes has PRIMARY KEY(call_id) — one scope per call site for ALL channels — so the walker multiplexes two id spaces by SIGN into one int field and drops the value-channel scope whenever an exception scope is also present. This is the shared-table decision's structural ceiling: it cannot hold N channels.
findings.evidence: arch_index_cmt.ml:2187-2193 — `let exn_scope = match exn_scope with | Some _ -> exn_scope | None -> (match Hashtbl.find_opt errch_call_scope ord with | Some (_, local_id) -> Some (-(local_id + 1)) (* negative: errch id-space marker *) | None -> None)`; architecture-schema.sql:389-392 `CREATE TABLE ... call_exn_scopes (call_id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY ...)`.
findings.fix: Change call_exn_scopes to PRIMARY KEY (call_id, scope_id) (additive within schema 1.6; the query already reads it via LEFT JOIN and the exception path selects scopes WHERE channel='exception', so a second row per call is invisible to it). Then delete the negative-id encoding: emit one row per (call, channel) and let the walker keep two independent Hashtbls without folding them. Cost: 1 schema line, ~8 lines in arch_index_cmt.ml (2187-2193 + 2861-2882 rewrite), 1 insert-site in arch_index.ml, no query change. Doing this now is far cheaper than after a third channel shape lands, and it removes the only place in the codebase where a row id's sign carries meaning.

findings.summary: The load-bearing portability claim fails: five of exn_edges' six roles are dead vocabulary. Only role='propagates' is ever written and only that role is ever read. Transforms, converters, sinks and binds are resolved entirely inside the OCaml walker and baked into exn_origins rows + edge presence/absence, so a Go/Rust/TS producer that follows docs/error-channels-porting.md §1 gets silent no-ops.
findings.evidence: arch_exn.ml:268 — `JOIN exn_edges ee ON ee.call_id=c.id AND ee.role='propagates' AND ee.channel=?` is the only read of exn_edges anywhere; arch_index.ml:833 `insert_exn_edge db stmt_edge ~call_id ~channel ~role:"propagates"` is the only write. architecture-schema.sql:408 declares `CHECK(role IN ('propagates','bind_arg','sink','transform_add','transform_replace','convert'))`. docs/error-channels-porting.md:33-35 instructs porters to record transform/converter/sink as those roles.
findings.fix: Either (a) honestly narrow the contract: drop bind_arg/sink/transform_add/transform_replace/convert from the CHECK, and rewrite docs/error-channels-porting.md:33-35 to say those four roles are resolved producer-side and must be expressed as exn_origins rows plus edge omission (one CHECK line, three doc rows); or (b) move transform/converter resolution into arch_exn.ml so the roles mean something. (a) costs ~10 lines and makes the doc true today; (b) is the real generalisation but is a follow-up feature. Do NOT ship the doc as written — it promises behaviour that does not exist.

findings.summary: Spec FR-025 and US-2.7 require the value-channel ⊤ reason token `unknown_error_value`; the implementation emits `unknown_exn_value` on every channel. Both docs/error-channels-porting.md and the fixture comment already document the spec token, so the docs are wrong about shipped behaviour and no test pins it.
findings.evidence: arch_exn.ml:36 `| Unknown_exn_value -> "unknown_exn_value"`, reached for value channels at arch_exn.ml:421 `| "unknown", _ | _, None -> join acc (top Unknown_exn_value ...)`. specs/error-channels.md:69 "`UNBOUNDED (⊤)` reason `unknown_error_value`"; docs/error-channels-porting.md:46 and :139 both say "⊤ `unknown_error_value`". No assertion on the token exists in tezt/tests/error_channels.ml (only the comment at :361).
findings.fix: Make reason_kind_to_string channel-aware: `Unknown_exn_value -> if channel = "exception" then "unknown_exn_value" else "unknown_error_value"`. reason_kind_to_string is called from arch_query.ml (error-stats dominant reason) and arch_exn.ml:512 reasons_of — thread `t.channel` through both (2 call sites, ~6 lines). AC-17 keeps the exception spelling byte-identical. Add the missing assertion to tezt/tests/error_channels.ml around :361.

findings.summary: Channel selection is first-match-wins over the merged channel list, so a channel whose carrier type duplicates an earlier one is structurally unreachable — yet it is still listed in error_contract, so every query on it answers NOT_A_CARRIER, which reads as a fact about the code rather than about the config. The shipped tzoption channel is exactly this case. The config layer can and should refuse it.
findings.evidence: profiles/tezos-errors.toml:151 `type = "option"` — identical to the built-in option channel's arch_errors_config.ml:80 `type_paths = ["option"; "Stdlib.option"]`. arch_index_errch.ml:52-60 `carrier_channel_of_type` uses `List.find_opt` over `channels`, and merge (arch_errors_config.ml:311-324) keeps built-ins first, so `option` always wins. arch_index.ml:586-588 `channel_emitted` only checks that a type_path was seen, so tzoption IS published in error_contract.
findings.fix: Add a post-merge check in Arch_errors_config.merge (or a new `check_disjoint : t -> (unit, string) result` called from arch_index.ml:548): if two channels share any type_path, fail with `arch-errors: channel tzoption: carrier type 'option' is already claimed by channel 'option' — it would never match`. ~15 lines plus one inline test. Then either delete [channel.tzoption] from the profile or give it a distinguishing carrier. A silently-inert config entry is precisely the bug class FR-023 exists to catch, so leaving it violates the feature's own stated purpose.

findings.summary: The `form` vocabulary is now incoherent: value-channel handler scopes are written as form='match_exception' and value-channel origins as form='raise', both untrue of a `match ... Error` / `Error A` construct. The exn_scopes CHECK was never widened, so a non-OCaml producer literally cannot record a value handler without lying — and any future form the query DOES read will be indistinguishable.
findings.evidence: architecture-schema.sql:359 `form TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(form IN ('try','match_exception'))` — unchanged. arch_index_cmt.ml:2831 `insert_exn_scope db stmt_scope ~function_id:fid ~parent_id:None ~form:"match_exception"` for value channels; arch_index_errch.ml:255 `let form = if form <> "" then form else if path = None then "unknown" else "raise"`. The justification at arch_index_cmt.ml:2806-2808 is "irrelevant at query time — Arch_exn.load never selects exn_scopes.form", which is true today and is exactly what makes the column silently rot.
findings.fix: Widen both CHECKs additively within schema 1.6 and use honest tokens: exn_scopes.form gains 'match_value' and 'declared_handler'; exn_origins.form gains 'error_value'. Cost: 2 CHECK lines, 2 literals in arch_index_cmt.ml (2831, and the default in arch_index_errch.ml:255), one docs/schema.md row edit, plus the enumeration in docs/error-channels-porting.md §4 which currently lists no allowed `form` values at all (:29). Cheaper now than after the first external producer hits a CHECK violation it cannot debug.

findings.summary: The channel record collapses three semantically distinct config keys — `type`, `underlying`, `aliases` — into one flat `type_paths` list, discarding which spelling matched. The arity check then has to guess, and unconditionally answers `true` whenever the matched constructor has fewer arguments than `error_arg`. Any type named in `underlying`/`aliases` with a mismatched arity becomes an unconditional carrier.
findings.evidence: arch_errors_config.ml:234 `type_paths = (type_ :: underlying) @ aliases;`. arch_index_errch.ml:41-42 — `match List.nth_opt args (pos - 1) with | None -> true (* shorter-arity alias: error type implied by the declaration *)`. Nothing distinguishes "the declaration's own 1-arg alias" from "a user typo'd `underlying` naming an unrelated 1-arg type".
findings.fix: Keep the three fields separate on the record (`carrier : string; underlying : string list; aliases : string list`) and give each its own arity/error_type expectation; derive `type_paths` as a function when a flat list is needed for validation (arch_errors_config.ml:413, arch_index_errch.ml:58). Cost: 1 record field split, ~6 call sites (:234, :357, :413, :446-451, arch_index_errch.ml:58, arch_index.ml:586). This also lets validate() report which of the three roles missed, which the current single warning cannot.

findings.summary: Merge is whole-channel replacement keyed by name, so a user cannot remove or amend a single built-in rule — to drop one entry from the built-in `result` channel's `binds` they must retype the whole channel, and the only way to disable a built-in channel is the undocumented accident of redeclaring it with a bogus `type` (non-fatal only because validate() exempts built-in names).
findings.evidence: arch_errors_config.ml:326-331 `merge` → `merge_named ~name_of:(fun (c : channel) -> c.name)`, and merge_named:313-314 `Hashtbl.replace tbl (name_of x) x` for base then override — the override's channel record wholly displaces the base's. arch_errors_config.ml:446 `if c.type_paths <> [] && !fatal = None && not (List.mem c.name builtin_names)` is what makes the disable-by-bogus-type trick non-fatal, and it is nowhere documented in docs/error-channels.md.
findings.fix: Add an explicit `enabled = false` key to the channel table (rejected today by reject_unknown_keys at :122-126) and filter disabled channels out of `value_channels` in arch_index.ml:472. ~12 lines + one known_channel_keys entry + one docs/error-channels.md paragraph. Per-rule subtraction (a `remove_binds = [...]` style key) is a larger design question and can stay a documented limitation — but the whole-channel-replace semantics must be stated in docs/error-channels.md, which currently does not mention it.

findings.summary: collect_calls_from_expr grew from 793 to 1385 lines in one function (+75%). It now hosts CFG lowering, exception scopes, carrier detection, bind/transform/converter/sink recognition and call collection in a single closure over ~20 mutable tables. This is the single largest maintainability regression in the diff.
findings.evidence: New: arch_index_cmt.ml:843 `let collect_calls_from_expr ...` to :2227 (next toplevel is `let process_cmt` at :2228) = 1385 lines. Base: origin/main's arch_index_cmt.ml:837 to :1629 = 793 lines. The value-channel-specific helpers alone (`resolve_head_call`, `mark_sunk`, `head_qualified_name`, `is_declared_bind`, `bare_ctor_name`, `find_transform`, `find_converter`, `carrier_of`) are all defined inline at :853-1200.
findings.fix: Move the pure, config-driven recognisers out to arch_index_errch.ml, which already owns the compiler-libs channel logic and is only 259 lines: `head_qualified_name`, `is_declared_bind`, `bare_ctor_name`, `find_transform`, `find_converter` take (channel list, head, expr) and return an option — none of them close over the walker's mutable state. That is roughly 120 lines relocated, mechanically, with no behaviour change, and it also puts the config-shaped predicates next to `carrier_channel_of_type` where a reader looks for them.

findings.summary: The schema file's own comments describe a state two slices out of date: they tell the reader the producer emits exception rows only, that exn_edges is unused, and that all of this is schema 1.3 (the version was renumbered to 1.6). The schema is the first thing a porter reads and it currently misinforms them about what is written.
findings.evidence: architecture-schema.sql:353 "The producer emits only 'exception' rows as of schema 1.3 (slices 0-1)"; :400-403 "Additive, unused as of schema 1.3: the producer emits every fact through exn_origins/exn_scopes/call_exn_scopes on the 'exception' channel only ...; value channels (result/option/...) start writing rows here in a later slice"; :418 "under schema 1.3". Contradicted by arch_index.ml:833 (exn_edges written) and arch_index_cmt.ml:2827-2851 (value-channel scopes and origins written). docs/schema.md:245 correctly says 1.6.
findings.fix: Rewrite the three comment blocks (architecture-schema.sql:351-354, 374, 396-403, 416-418) to describe schema 1.6 as shipped, and state in the exn_edges comment that only 'propagates' is currently produced and consumed. ~12 comment lines in one file.

findings.summary: Naming debt is now user-visible, not merely internal. The module, its tables and its refusal messages all say `exn`, and a value-channel query on a table-less DB prints an exception-worded message telling the user to rebuild to get raises/raisers-of/exn-stats — commands that have nothing to do with the channel they asked about.
findings.evidence: arch_exn.ml:91-93 `let not_analysed = "NOT_ANALYSED: this index has no exception sites (its producer did not emit them). Rebuild with arch-callgraph-ocaml — the CMT producer — to get raises / raisers-of / exn-stats."`, reached for value channels at arch_exn.ml:219 `if not (Arch_db.has_table t "exn_origins") then Arch_db.refuse "%s" not_analysed`. Compare :202-206, where the value-channel path DOES have a correctly-worded message (`not_analysed_channel`).
findings.fix: Two tiers. Cheap and worth doing now: parameterise `not_analysed` by channel so the :219 refusal names the channel and may-fail rather than raises (≈6 lines, 1 file). Expensive and NOT worth doing now: renaming Arch_exn/arch_index_exn/exn_* tables — that is 5 table names across architecture-schema.sql, arch_index_db.ml/.mli, arch_index.ml, arch_exn.ml, arch_load.ml plus every DB in existence, with no query-visible benefit. Record it as a documented residual in docs/error-channels.md instead: one paragraph stating that the `exn_*` prefix is historical and means "error channel", so the next reader is not left to infer it from arch_exn.ml:196-201's comment.

findings.summary: The --channel / positional-argument parser is copy-pasted three times across may-fail, fails-with and error-stats, with the three copies already differing in behaviour (may-fail dies without --channel, fails-with silently defaults to exception, error-stats dies). They will drift further the moment a fourth flag is added.
findings.evidence: bin/arch_query/arch_query.ml:659-681 (may-fail), :726-748 (fails-with), :776-786 (error-stats) each define `let rec find = function | "--channel" :: c :: _ -> Some c | _ :: tl -> find tl | [] -> None`; two of the three then repeat the same 8-line `drop` for positionals.
findings.fix: Hoist one `let channel_and_positionals ?default rest = ...` above the subcommand match (the `channels_of_contract` helper at :146 is already there and is the natural neighbour) and call it three times. Removes ~40 duplicated lines, and forces the default-vs-required difference to be an explicit argument rather than an accident.

findings.summary: The [summaries] table crosses the producer/query boundary through a bespoke TAB/pipe/colon text format with a hand-rolled encoder and a hand-rolled decoder in two libraries, no shared definition and no round-trip test — even though arch_tools already links yojson and could have used JSON.
findings.evidence: Encoder arch_index.ml:569-577 (`callee ^ "\t" ^ String.concat "|" (List.map (fun (c, paths) -> c ^ ":" ^ String.concat "," paths) chans)`); decoder arch_exn.ml:139-165 `decode_summaries`. The justification at arch_index.ml:561-567 is that Arch_exn must not depend on otoml — true, but lib/arch_tools/dune already lists `yojson`, so that constraint did not force a custom format.
findings.fix: Serialise as a JSON object `{"<callee>": {"<channel>": ["path", ...]}}` — yojson is already a dependency of both libraries. ~10 lines each side, and the format becomes self-describing for anyone inspecting comment_db_meta by hand. If the text format is kept, add a round-trip inline test pairing the two functions; there is none today, and the "no escaping is needed" claim at arch_index.ml:566 is asserted, not tested.

findings.summary: `contribution` applies the hardcoded OCaml Stdlib `known_leaf` table on every channel, though the table's entries are justified by exception semantics ("effect recorded as an origin", "cannot raise"). The neighbouring `builtin_stdlib_summaries` is correctly gated on channel='exception'; this one is not, so the two OCaml-specific tables in the same file disagree on whether channel matters.
findings.evidence: arch_exn.ml:428-438 `contribution` — `if known_leaf name then Known SS.empty` with no channel test; contrast arch_exn.ml:343 `if use_builtin_summaries && channel = "exception" then ...`. known_leaf's own docstring at :95-105 is entirely about raising: "primitives that cannot raise", "Everything else outside the index ... is ⊤ [external]".
findings.fix: Gate it: `if t.channel = "exception" && known_leaf name then ...`. One line. Today the practical effect is near-nil (none of the listed Stdlib primitives returns a result/option carrier, so few value-channel edges reach it), which is why this is LOW rather than HIGH — but it is the concrete counter-example to docs/error-channels-porting.md:9's "Nothing in the query layer is OCaml-specific", and gating it makes that sentence closer to true at negligible cost.

findings.summary: `escapes` and `scope_id` mean different things per channel in the same table: exception origins compute both from the scope chain, value-channel origins are hardcoded `~escapes:true ~scope_id:None`. A reader (or a porter) inspecting exn_origins cannot tell that the columns are only meaningful for one channel.
findings.evidence: arch_index_cmt.ml:2846-2850 `insert_exn_origin db stmt_origin ~function_id:fid ~scope_id:None ~form:o.o_form ~exn_path:o.o_path ~escapes:true ~line:o.o_line ~col:o.o_col ~channel:o.o_channel` — compare :2792-2797 where the exception path passes computed `~scope_id` and `~escapes:o.o_escapes`. The value-channel origin record (arch_index_errch.ml:207-218) has no `o_escapes`/`o_scope` field at all.
findings.fix: The over-approximation is sound (arch_exn.ml:418 only skips non-escaping origins, so escapes=true can only widen the set), so this is a documentation debt rather than a defect: add the constraint to architecture-schema.sql's exn_origins comment ("escapes/scope_id are computed only on channel='exception'; value channels always record escapes=1, scope_id NULL") and to docs/error-channels-porting.md:29's row. ~4 lines. Alternatively make the errch accumulator compute escapes from its own flat scope list, which would be the real generalisation but is a behaviour change needing its own oracle.

findings.summary: The validation `seen` table is keyed by path string globally, not per channel, so two channels declaring the same path share one found-flag. A path that only ever occurs in channel A's carrier context still marks channel B's identical declaration as matched, suppressing the warning FR-023 exists to produce.
findings.evidence: arch_errors_config.ml:405-417 `create` builds a single `values` and a single `types` Hashtbl by iterating all channels: `List.iter (fun p -> if not (Hashtbl.mem values p) then Hashtbl.replace values p (ref false)) (declared_value_paths c)`. arch_errors_config.ml:459-473 then reads those shared flags per channel to emit `channel %s: '%s' matched nothing`.
findings.fix: Key the tables by (channel_name, path) and have note_value_path/note_type_path mark every channel whose declaration matches. ~20 lines in arch_errors_config.ml:389-439, plus threading the channel through the two note_* call sites in arch_index_cmt.ml. This is the same root cause as the tzoption finding — the config layer has no per-channel view of what actually matched — so fixing both together is cheaper than either alone.

findings.summary: Two parallel fact accumulators exist — Arch_index_exn and Arch_index_errch — with independently-defined origin/scope/acc types and a byte-identical `pos` helper, writing into the same tables through the same prepared statements. They are not a generalised mechanism; the drift risk is real but the record shapes genuinely differ (exn scopes nest and carry a form variant, value scopes are flat and untyped), so unifying them is not obviously right.
findings.evidence: arch_index_errch.ml:207-259 defines `type origin`, `type scope`, `type acc`, `create`, `pos`, `add_scope`, `add_origin`, `finalize`; arch_index_exn.ml:51-84, :269, :281, :397 define the same seven names. arch_index_errch.ml:233-235 `let pos (loc : Location.t) = let p = loc.loc_start in (p.pos_lnum, p.pos_cnum - p.pos_bol + 1)` is character-for-character arch_index_exn.ml:269-271.
findings.fix: Do not unify the record types — the nesting difference is real. Do share the one thing that is actually identical: move `pos` to Arch_index_support (or expose Arch_index_exn.pos) and delete the copy at arch_index_errch.ml:233. Two lines. Record the parallel-accumulator structure as a known duplication in docs/error-channels.md so the next person adding a channel role knows both modules exist rather than discovering the second one by grep.

git show origin/main:lib/arch_index/arch_index_db.ml | grep 'let current_schema_version' -> `let current_schema_version = "1.7"`.
Branch: lib/arch_index/arch_index_db.ml:52 -> `let current_schema_version = "1.6"`.
git merge-base HEAD origin/main = 2a82b9f (whose value is "1.5"); `git rev-list --count HEAD..origin/main` = 1 (ef57163 'feat(schema): calls.top_reason/top_anchor' bumped 1.5 -> 1.7).

findings.summary: FR-027 VIOLATED: channel selection is first-match-wins (List.find_opt), so a function is a carrier of at most ONE channel. The spec's carrier check is per-channel ('a function node is a c-carrier iff ...'). The shipped profile's `tzoption` is therefore structurally dead, yet it IS advertised in error_contract — so a query on it answers NOT_A_CARRIER (a positive claim) instead of NOT_ANALYSED, which is exactly the 'empty set vs nobody looked' confusion this feature exists to prevent.
findings.evidence:
lib/arch_index/arch_index_errch.ml:52-60 — `let carrier_channel_of_type ~channels ty = ... List.find_opt (fun c -> ...) channels` returns at most one channel; lib/arch_index/arch_index_cmt.ml:853 `let carrier_of ty = Arch_index_errch.carrier_channel_of_type ~channels:value_channels ty`.
Ran on proto_alpha with --errors-profile tezos (fresh DB, exit 0):

findings.summary: [new] A matched constructor's OWN argument pattern is ignored when the arm's caught identity is computed, so a narrowed pattern (`Error (B 0)`, `Error (B (0 | 1))`, `try ... with B 0 -> ...`) is credited with catching every value of that constructor. An error the call can still return disappears from a BOUNDED answer. Same class as the round-1 CRITICAL, different mechanism, and it affects the value channels AND the frozen exception channel.
findings.evidence: lib/arch_index/arch_index_errch.ml:116-121 `literal_ctor_path_of_pat` returns `Some (constructor_canonical_path ...)` for any `Tpat_construct`, discarding the sub-pattern list; it is consumed at lib/arch_index/arch_index_errch.ml:193 as `Some pth -> Caught pth`. The exception channel has the identical defect at lib/arch_index/arch_index_exn.ml:220-221 `| Tpat_construct (_, {cstr_tag = Cstr_extension (path, _); _}, _, _) -> {caught = [canon path]; catch_all = false; bound = []}` (third field, the sub-patterns, bound to `_`). REPRODUCED, built-in `result` channel, fixture /mnt/ssd-external-2to/arch-index-runs/r2-1788476294-narrow/proj: `let f n : (int, err) result = if n = 0 then Error A else if n = 1 then Error (B 7) else Error C`; `let h_narrow () = match f 0 with Error (B 0) -> Ok 0 | r -> r` and `let h_narrow_or () = match f 0 with Error (B (0 | 1)) -> Ok 0 | r -> r` both answer `BOUNDED: {Nb.A, Nb.C}` while the control `Error (B _)` answers the same — i.e. `Nb.B` is closed although `Error (B 7)` reaches `| r -> r` and is re-returned. Command: `ARCH_QUERY_FORMAT=list _build/default/bin/arch_query/arch_query.exe /mnt/ssd-external-2to/arch-index-runs/r2-1788476294-narrow/n.db may-fail h_narrow --channel result`. REPRODUCED on the exception channel, fixture /mnt/ssd-external-2to/arch-index-runs/r2-exnpat/proj: `exception B of int`, `f` raises `A`, `B 7`, `C`; `let h_narrow n = try f n with B 0 -> ()` answers `raises h_narrow -> BOUNDED: {Xp.A, Xp.C}` — `Xp.B` dropped. The or-pattern controls are correct on both channels (`h_or`/`g_or` keep every unmatched identity), so this is specifically the constructor-argument case the round-1 fix did not cover.
findings.fix: An arm may only be credited with catching identity `K` when every argument pattern under `K` is irrefutable — `Tpat_any`, `Tpat_var`, an alias over one, or a tuple/record whose fields are all irrefutable. Otherwise the arm matches an unnameable subset of `K`: on the value channel return `Unrecognised` (closes nothing), on the exception channel contribute nothing to `caught` and do not set `catch_all`. Concretely: give `literal_ctor_path_of_pat` an `~irrefutable_args_only:true` mode used by the classifier (leave the origin-side expression variant alone), and make `arch_index_exn.ml`'s `pat_class` inspect the `Tpat_construct` sub-pattern list it currently ignores. Add tezt cases for `Error (B 0)` / `try ... with B 0 -> ()` asserting the constructor SURVIVES.

Extend the new 're-indexing an existing database is idempotent' tezt (tezt/tests/error_channels.ml:499) to a fixture that produces dead-code rows, and assert the count over EVERY table the producer writes rather than only the exn/errch ones — the round-1 defect and this one are both 'a table nobody added to the list', and only a table-agnostic assertion catches the next one.

findings.summary: [new] The new reachability refusal makes §4's escape hatch unusable in the common case: 'Two channels over one carrier type are fine when a distinguishing `error_type`/`error_arg` tells them apart' is false whenever the earlier channel is an untouched built-in, because a built-in applies no argument test and therefore claims everything. The refusal then tells the operator to 'Reorder the channels', which is not expressible — built-ins are always merged first.
findings.evidence: lib/arch_index/arch_errors_config.ml:480-490 `claims`: `no_narrower_test` is true when `earlier.error_arg = None || earlier.error_type = None || ...`, and the built-in `result`/`option` channels declare neither. findings.evidence: REPRODUCED. Extracted the profile's `[channel.option]` block verbatim (profiles/tezos-errors.toml:159-180) into a standalone config and ran `arch_callgraph_ocaml -b _build/default --errors-config <block> --errors-strict` against this repository: exit 1, `arch-errors: --errors-strict: 9 declaration(s) matched nothing`. Five of the nine are paths the profile RESTATED from the built-in and would have been waived otherwise: `Stdlib.Option.get`, `Stdlib.Option.fold`, `Stdlib.Option.Syntax.let*`, `Stdlib.Option.Syntax.and*`, `Stdlib.option`. Independently confirmed the premise on a clean built-in run of the same corpus: `comment_db_meta.error_config_unmatched` = `...,Stdlib.option` while bare `option` is absent, i.e. `Stdlib.option` really is unmatchable — exactly as lib/arch_index/arch_errors_config.ml:583-587 claims. No test covers this: tezt/tests/error_channels.ml:136-160 exercises strict only against a synthetic `errch_strict_ok` fixture, never against `--errors-profile tezos`.
findings.fix: Two independent repairs, either of which closes it. (a) Delete `Stdlib.option` from lib/arch_index/arch_errors_config.ml:80 and from profiles/tezos-errors.toml:161 — it is a declaration that is wrong, not a declaration the waiver should hide, and removing it is a one-line change in each file. (b) Replace structural-equality waiving with per-path provenance: tag each path at merge time with whether it came from `builtin` or from a file (one bool alongside the string in the channel's lists), so a restated built-in path stays waived and a path the operator actually wrote never is — that is what `is_untouched_builtin` is trying and failing to approximate. Then add a tezt case asserting `--errors-profile tezos --errors-strict` exit code, so the claim is pinned.

findings.summary: [fix-incomplete] 'Structural equality with a built-in' is a trap, not a rule. The waiver boundary is defined by OCaml constants in this file, so an unrelated edit to `result_channel` or `option_channel` silently moves every user profile across it — a config that passed CI yesterday fails today with no config change. It has already sprung once inside this branch (see the tezos-profile finding).
findings.evidence: lib/arch_index/arch_errors_config.ml:540-546 `is_untouched_builtin` compares `canon_channel b = canon_channel c` against lib/arch_index/arch_errors_config.ml:97 `builtin`. `canon_channel` (arch_errors_config.ml:341-352) hashes every declared list, so adding one path to `result_channel` (arch_errors_config.ml:52-75) or `option_channel` (arch_errors_config.ml:77-95) flips any profile that had been byte-equal from waived to fully strict-responsible. The rule is also all-or-nothing at channel granularity: adding a single sink to `[channel.option]` makes the operator answerable for six `Stdlib.*` paths they never wrote. The .mli (lib/arch_index/arch_errors_config.mli:132-142) and docs/error-channels.md:264-268 both document the rule as intentional, so a reader will not suspect the boundary moves.
findings.fix: Track provenance per path rather than inferring it from whole-channel structural equality: carry `(path, from_builtin : bool)` through `merge` (arch_errors_config.ml:311-331) and filter `operator_warnings` (arch_errors_config.ml:588-591) on that flag. That makes the rule stateable in one sentence a config author can act on ('paths you wrote are strict; paths you inherited are not'), independent of what the built-in table happens to contain. Touches the `channel` record, `merge_named`, `create`, `validate` and the six built-in constants — one file, roughly 60 lines.

findings.summary: [new] `check_reachable` is at the right LAYER (config-only, before any .cmt is read, one call site) but it patches an ordering rule that should not exist, and its remedy text offers an action the format cannot deliver. 'First-match-wins plus a refusal' makes declaration order semantically load-bearing and user-visible, while the order itself is not something a config author controls.
findings.evidence: lib/arch_index/arch_errors_config.ml:531-537 tells the user to 'Reorder the channels so the more specific one comes first, or merge the two declarations into one.' Reordering is impossible in the only case that has actually occurred: `merge` composes builtin < profile < user with base first (lib/arch_index/arch_errors_config.ml:311-324 `base @ override`), so no file-declared channel can ever precede a built-in — which is why the Tezos profile had to take the 'merge' branch and duplicate the built-in (previous finding). Within a single file, order comes from iterating otoml's `[channel]` table (lib/arch_index/arch_errors_config.ml:259-262); TOML tables are unordered by specification and nothing in the tree pins otoml's iteration order, so a rule whose remedy is 'reorder' rests on an untested parser property. The narrowing that creates all of this is first-match-wins carrier selection, which the branch has now written back into the spec (specs/error-channels.md FR-027 'Narrowing, review round 1') — spec following implementation.
findings.fix: Prefer either: (a) most-specific-match selection — rank candidate channels by the specificity of the matching `type_paths` entry (literal beats wildcard, longer qualified path beats shorter) and then by whether `error_type`/`error_arg` apply a test, picking the maximum; ties are the only thing that needs refusing, and the rule is one sentence with no ordering in it; or (b) per-channel carrier membership as FR-027 originally specified, which removes selection entirely. Either removes `check_reachable` (arch_errors_config.ml:479-537, ~60 lines incl. tests), the arch_index.ml:236-241 exit, the FR-023b/FR-027 spec amendments, and the profile duplication. If `check_reachable` is kept for this ship, at least fix the message: drop 'Reorder the channels' when the earlier channel is a built-in, since that instruction cannot be followed, and add an inline test pinning that `of_toml` preserves document order for `[channel.*]`.

findings.summary: [fix-incomplete] `caught_class` is correct but is the wrong of two equally cheap shapes. `Caught of string list` is strictly more precise, subsumes the three-case type (`Unrecognised` is exactly `Caught []`), and costs essentially nothing to adopt because everything downstream is ALREADY set-valued. findings.summary: [fix-incomplete] FR-024 still PARTIAL (unchanged since round 1): `error_config_digest` is MD5 (OCaml's Digest), not the SHA-256 the spec names. JUDGEMENT: this is a spec/code mismatch worth closing in the CODE, not a spec defect to wave through — the substantive properties hold, but the fix is ~2 lines and 'SHA-256' in a contract will keep drawing review fire.
findings.evidence:
lib/arch_index/arch_errors_config.ml:334 comment 'Digest — canonical structural serialisation, MD5 hex'; :383 `Digest.to_hex (Digest.string (chan_str ^ "##" ^ sum_str))` — OCaml's Digest is MD5. Unchanged by this round's commits.
Observed digests are 32 hex chars (SHA-256 would be 64):
  sqlite3 /mnt/ssd-external-2to/arch-index-runs/r2-self.db "select key, value, length(value) from comment_db_meta where key like 'error_config%'"
    -> error_config_digest|21edc0e390cb898e022dcfcc73bc3d20|32
  and on the proto_alpha profile run -> ae45b757d6457018049ca9f4d8a9152e (32)
specs/error-channels.md:28 is unchanged: '`error_config_digest` = SHA-256 of the canonical serialisation of the *effective merged* config (sorted keys)'.
The two properties FR-024 actually depends on DO hold and I re-verified them: effective-merged (builtin-only 21edc0e3… differs from builtin+tezos-profile ae45b757…), and stability across reformatting (verified round 1; the serialisation code is untouched since).
WHICH SHOULD CHANGE — the code. The digest's job is to tell two effective configs apart in comment_db_meta, and for that a 128-bit content hash is functionally adequate; MD5's collision weakness is not in this threat model, so this is NOT a soundness bug and NOT ship-blocking. But 'adequate' is the only argument for keeping it: the switch already carries digestif/mirage-crypto, the call site is one expression, and nothing depends on the current value (producers always rebuild the DB, so no stored digest needs migrating). Weakening the spec to 'a stable content digest' buys nothing and loses a property that costs nothing to hold — and leaves a hash a future reader may reasonably mistake for a provenance token. Amending the spec is an acceptable second choice ONLY if paired with an explicit 'not an integrity token' note.
findings.fix: Replace `Digest.to_hex (Digest.string s)` at lib/arch_index/arch_errors_config.ml:383 with a SHA-256 hex over the same canonical string (digestif or mirage-crypto, both already in the switch), and update the :334 comment. No migration needed — producers always rebuild. Alternatively amend specs/error-channels.md:28 to 'a stable content digest of the effective merged config (not an integrity token)'.

findings.summary: [new-finding, pre-existing since slice 2, SOUND direction] A value-channel match arm whose or-pattern sits ACROSS the origin constructor (`Error A | Error C -> ...`) is skipped entirely, so it closes nothing; and `Error A | _ -> ...` mints no scope at all instead of closing the channel. Only or-patterns UNDER the constructor (`Error (A | C)`) are classified. This is over-approximation, never unsound — but it is the exact second form the round-1 CRITICAL's own fix direction named ("Add tezt cases for `Error (A | B) -> ...` and `Error A | Error B -> ...`"), it has no test, and it is not listed among the residuals in docs/error-channels.md §6.
findings.evidence: REPRODUCED on /mnt/ssd-external-2to/arch-index-runs/r3-probe6 (probe6/pg.ml, `type err = A | B of int | C`, `multi n` returning all three). `let top_or n = match multi n with Error A | Error C -> Ok 0 | r -> r` -> `arch-query may-fail top_or --channel result` = `BOUNDED: {Pg.A, Pg.B, Pg.C}` (expected `{Pg.B}`); `let top_or2 n = match multi n with Error A | _ -> Ok 0` = `BOUNDED: {Pg.A, Pg.B, Pg.C}` (expected `{}`). Confirmed in the database: `SELECT f.name, s.id, s.catch_all, group_concat(c.exn_path) FROM exn_scopes s JOIN functions f ON f.id=s.function_id LEFT JOIN exn_scope_catches c ON c.scope_id=s.id` gives top_or scope id 6 with catch_all=0 and NO caught rows, and top_or2 no scope row at all (its call to `multi` has a NULL scope_id in call_exn_scopes). Mechanism is documented in the code itself at lib/arch_index/arch_index_cmt.ml:1500-1506 -- `value_arms` keeps only `Tpat_value` computation cases, and a source-level `p1 | p2` arm is a computation-level `Tpat_or`, which the filter_map drops: "An [exception]/or-pattern computation case never matches an origin constructor, so it is simply skipped (safe: a skipped arm cannot close anything, the over-approximating direction)." Introduced by 4b73961 (slice 2), i.e. pre-existing, not a round-3 regression. Contrast the exception channel, which DOES flatten computation-level or-patterns (lib/arch_index/arch_index_exn.ml:279-283) -- verified: `try raiser n with Boom _ | EA _ -> ()` = `BOUNDED: {}` and `with Boom 0 | EA _ -> ()` = `BOUNDED: {Pg.Boom}`, both correct. The two channels therefore disagree on the same source shape.
findings.fix: Flatten the computation-level `Tpat_or` in the `value_arms` filter_map exactly as `Arch_index_exn.exception_arms` already does for the exception side: map one computation case to the LIST of its `Tpat_value` leaves, classify each, and union the results for that arm (a leaf that classifies to `None` must make the whole arm non-closing, not merely be dropped, so the union stays sound). Add tezt cases for `Error A | Error C` (expect the union closed) and `Error A | _` (expect catch-all). If that is deliberately out of scope, add the shape to docs/error-channels.md §6 Residuals so an operator is not surprised by `Error A | Error B` behaving differently from `Error (A | B)`.

findings.summary: [fix-verified-with-regression] 'Extend by default, [summaries] replaces' is a coherent and well-explained rule, and it closes my round-1 finding for the BUILT-IN layer (a profile can now amend a built-in without restating it). But the rule is uniform across all three layers while its justification covers only one, and it silently REMOVED a capability that existed before this round: under the old replace semantics a user file could drop a wrong PROFILE rule by redeclaring the channel; it now cannot drop anything, at any layer, and no removal syntax exists.
findings.evidence: lib/arch_index/arch_errors_config.ml:355-368 `merge_channel` is `dedup (base.X @ over.X)` for every list field, with the rationale at :344-352: 'Nothing can be REMOVED from a built-in this way — deliberate: a built-in's vocabulary is Stdlib paths that are true wherever they occur, so subtraction has no use case.' That argument is sound for the built-ins — every path in `result_channel`/`option_channel` (:52-95) is a literal `Stdlib.*` canonical path. It does not transfer to the profile layer, which `merge` treats identically: lib/arch_index/arch_index.ml:181/192 apply the same `Arch_errors_config.merge` for builtin<profile and profile<user, and profiles/tezos-errors.toml declares GLOB paths, e.g. `Tezos_protocol_environment_*.Error_monad.Option_syntax.let*` (:169-172) plus globbed `sinks`, which `path_matches`'s `*` crosses `.` boundaries with (round-1 finding, still open). Both are dispositioned in the QA scope as documented residuals, but the spec's C-19 and US-4.3 still say every answer must match and 'any mismatch is a soundness NO-GO, not a note'. Both mismatches are over-approximating or model-level, so neither is a soundness bug; the divergence is between the oracle rule as written and how it is being applied.

O-6 `may-fail begin_application` — three rows, id-ordered 254 (apply.ml) / 2413 (main.ml) / 7735 (validate.ml); the main.ml row is UNBOUNDED (⊤) with a large non-empty known part (Script_tc_errors.*, Contract_storage.Balance_too_low, Tez_repr.*) and may_top_edge witnesses in alpha_context.ml/script_ir_translator.ml — MATCH.
O-7 MISMATCH, unchanged: `SELECT id, name, path FROM functions JOIN modules …` shows main.ml carries apply_operation (id 2414) and finalize_application (id 2415) and NO finalize_block; both main.ml nodes have 0 outgoing calls rows and answer 'BOUNDED: {}', because they are point-free re-exports (`let f = M.g`, no Texp_apply) and the shared whole-repo walker only records an edge at an application site. The real Apply.apply_operation / Apply.finalize_block bodies DO carry the expected ⊤ witnesses.
findings.fix: Two options, both cheap: (1) re-word the O-5 and O-7 rows as EXPECTED residuals with the reason recorded, and amend C-19/US-4.3 to 'every answer matches the oracle, or the row is re-baselined against a recorded, sound-over-approximating residual signed off in the QA brief' — the O-7 root cause is a pre-existing property of the shared call-graph model on point-free aliases and is not an error-channels defect; or (2) replace O-7's named functions with the Apply.* bodies they forward to, which is what the oracle's own rationale ('nothing escapes to the shell') actually wanted to measure. O-5's exception half stays open until FR-025 (b) is either implemented or written down as a residual.
